decision: derive Phase-1 deployment manifest from verified Qubes policy and service-handler evidence before any qrexec invocation

artifactBoundQualification.correctness: strong: binds readiness to the exact persistent dom0 policy rule and coordinator qrexec service endpoint
artifactBoundQualification.robustnessSecurity: strong: empty-argument only allow, exact source/target/user binding, explicit catch-all deny, immutable service handler evidence
artifactBoundQualification.latency: negligible local parsing only; zero additional qrexec round trips
artifactBoundQualification.resourceUse: no daemon, watcher, database, WAL, or persistent runtime state
artifactBoundQualification.regressionRisk: low: additive deployment boundary reuses the existing manifest and Phase-1 runner contracts
artifactBoundQualification.qa: dedicated positive and fail-before-qrexec regressions plus workflow syntax coverage

handAuthoredManifestOnly.correctness: weaker: validates declared intent but not the deployed Qubes policy/service artifacts
handAuthoredManifestOnly.robustnessSecurity: can pass while dom0 policy or coordinator service handler has drifted
handAuthoredManifestOnly.qa: schema-only evidence cannot establish deployment provenance

persistentWatcherOrSupervisor.correctness: can observe runtime changes but does not improve policy provenance by itself
persistentWatcherOrSupervisor.robustnessSecurity: adds privileged lifecycle and IPC surface

failuresLessons: A valid Node manifest is not proof that the dom0 qrexec policy grants only the intended path.
For a no-argument read-only service, Qubes policy should allow the empty argument token '+' from exactly one source to exactly one coordinator and then deny all other calls to that service.
Deployment evidence must bind the service handler target to the exact candidate Git SHA and prove the service identity cannot rewrite it.
Keep real-Qubes Phase-1 read-only; do not use state-changing MissionQueue operations to validate policy routing.
safety: synthetic/defensive qualification only; no real financial transactions, payment data, fraud workflow, or weakened security controls
